reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: What is the total value of 1 ₱50 bill, 1 ₱5 coin, and 1 ₱1 coin?
What is the total value of 1 ₱10 coin and 1 ₱1 coin?
What is the total value of 1 ₱5 coin and 1 ₱1 coin?
What is the total value of 2 ₱1 coins?
What is the total value of 2 ₱20 bills and 1 ₱5 coin?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The money stems do what the verb asks and every total hand-checks: seed 42 gives 50 + 5 + 1 = 56, seed 43 gives 10 + 1 = 11, seed 44 gives 5 + 1 = 6, seed 45 gives 1 + 1 = 2, and seed 46 gives 20 + 20 + 5 = 45, all keyed correctly.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The wording explicitly enumerates four sub-cases and only two are generated: peso coins only (seeds 43, 44, 45) and combined coins with bills (seeds 42, 46). No centavo-coins-only item and no peso-bills-only item appears anywhere in the packet.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Piece counts stay at one or two per denomination and totals stay under 60 pesos, so a Grade 2 Quarter 2 pupil adds at most three friendly addends (50 + 5 + 1) with no regrouping and a single short sentence to read.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every stem is the identical 'What is the total value of ...' frame. There is no wallet or shopping context, no 'write the amount using the peso sign', and no item using several pieces of one denomination beyond the two 20-peso bills of seed 46.

competency_alignment.rationale: The five seeds cluster between 2 and 56 pesos with the same one-step summing demand, so there is no ladder from single-denomination counting up through mixed sets toward the 1000-peso combinations the competency envisions.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The stated ceiling is 1000 pesos but the largest total shown is 56 pesos and no denomination above the 50-peso bill of seed 42 ever appears; 100, 200, 500 and 1000-peso bills are entirely untested in this sample.
